research.title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
research.why: A plain-language finding about AI that a general reader can follow: reasoning models told to skip thinking keep thinking anyway. That affects cost, speed and how well users can control the model. It isn't an agent paper, so it doesn't repeat the Oct 10 tool-using-agents topic. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. HF listed it Oct 13 (arXiv ~Oct 8-9). 215 HF upvotes.

news.title: Anthropic: small AI models may be months from self-replicating on everyday devices
news.why: Highest significance for a general reader. Evaluations show a 9B model getting inference running on 8 of 9 hardware types, and stronger models (e.g. GLM-5.2) completing simplified end-to-end replication. Small models are projected to match by year end. It also breaks a run of model-launch news topics (Gemini 4 Argon, Mistral Large 4, Gemini agent). Writer notes: this is a self-reported company evaluation, so present it as Anthropic's claims and projections, not settled fact. Say 'simplified' replication. Avoid alarmist framing and any policy or regulation angle. Published Oct 12. HN 106 pts / 108 comments.

invention.title: Plimsoll: a sandbox that stamps every agent-code run with its isolation strength and refuses weaker sandboxes
invention.why: Most novel idea in the pool and of real practical importance. Each result records how strongly it was isolated (process, container, kernel, VM). A request can demand a minimum level, and if it can't be met, nothing runs. It also ties in naturally with the containment theme of the news pick. Caveat: low HN signal (16 pts / 4 comments) and a young self-hosted Go project. Describe what the README says it does, not proven adoption. Posted Oct 11.

invention.rejected: PDF TO MP3: commercial service with pricing, so it risks looking like paid placement. Mira walking tours: geographic. BetterWispr: crowded category.

thread: All three stories are about whether AI stays inside the limits people set: reasoning models that keep thinking after being told to stop, small models learning to copy themselves onto new hardware, and a sandbox that won't run agent code unless its walls are strong enough.
